entities.summary: Agathinus was an ancient Greek physician who founded the medical sect of Episynthetici, revolutionizing medical practices in the Roman Empire. Born in Greece around 25 CE, Agathinus traveled extensively throughout the Mediterranean, studying under prominent physicians and observing the healing practices of various cultures. His extensive travels and research led him to develop a comprehensive system of medicine, which he detailed in his seminal work, 'De Medicina.' This work, written in Greek and Latin, became a foundational text for medical education for centuries, influencing the development of Western medicine. Agathinus's contributions to medicine extended beyond his written works, as he established a network of medical schools and clinics throughout the empire, providing training and care to thousands of patients. Despite his significant impact on the field, Agathinus's life and work remain somewhat obscure, overshadowed by the more famous physicians of his time. Nevertheless, his legacy continues to shape the practice of medicine, with his ideas on diagnosis, treatment, and preventative care remaining relevant to this day.
